stem:
Gauri melts some wax, then lets it cool until it is solid again. She also chops a carrot into pieces.

Which judgment about these changes is correct?

options.text: Melting the wax is reversible, because the wax can be brought back in its starting solid form.
Chopping the carrot is reversible, because the carrot material is still there.
Melting the wax is not reversible, because melted wax looks different from solid wax.
Both changes are reversible, because both happen in the kitchen.

teacher.key_rationale: A change is reversible when the starting form can be recovered, so melted wax that solidifies again is reversible. Keeping the material after chopping is not recovery of starting form; calling melting irreversible reverses the recovery test.
